data.summary: The pod startup exceeded its SLO of 10.0 seconds, taking 65.0 seconds to become Ready. The primary cause was a slow readiness phase, which accounted for 58.931 seconds of the total time. This delay was due to the readiness probe's initialDelaySeconds being set to 45 seconds, despite the application reporting its startup complete much earlier.

findings.statement: The pod took 65.0 seconds to become Ready, exceeding the SLO of 10.0 seconds.
The readiness phase was the longest part of the startup, lasting 58.931 seconds.
The readiness probe was configured with an initialDelaySeconds of 45 seconds and a periodSeconds of 20 seconds.
The application reported 'startup_complete' after approximately 1.079 seconds from container start, indicating it was ready much earlier than Kubernetes marked the pod Ready.
There were no probe failures after the application reported itself ready.

ruled_out.reason: The scheduling phase duration was 0.0 seconds, and there were no failed scheduling events.
The image pull duration was 4.141 seconds for 53328919 bytes, with a throughput of 12878271 bytes/s, which is not excessively slow or large enough to be the primary cause of the 65.0 second startup.
The image pull throughput was 12878271 bytes/s, which is not indicative of a slow registry or network.
The model loading time (model_s) was 0.0 seconds.
The app_init phase lasted only 0.928 seconds, and the application logs show 'startup_complete' very early, indicating the application itself was not slow to initialise.

recommendations.rationale: The application reports 'startup_complete' very quickly, so the initialDelaySeconds of 45 seconds is unnecessarily prolonging the readiness phase. Adjusting this value will allow the pod to become Ready sooner.
